target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution already emits diagnostics when a configured SecretRef fails and provider env credentials are used instead (for example web-search/web-fetch fallback warnings and gateway token env fallback), but `openclaw security audit` and doctor did not surface that boundary drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a config-layer plugin load path collector that reuses existing discovery and doctor bundled-path helpers, then maps results to structured security audit findings (`plugins.load_paths.*`). Added a shared secrets diagnostic helper (`collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics`) used by both security audit (`secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`) and a new doctor health check (`core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`). This keeps runtime behavior unchanged while aligning audit/doctor output with existing runtime warnings.

The deep skill code-safety scan (`collectInstalledSkillsCodeSafetyFindings`) retains `includeArchived: true` so archived workspace skills continue to be inspected for code-safety findings, matching current `main` behavior.

## User Impact

* Operators running `openclaw security audit` now get early warnings when `plugins.load.paths` points at risky or missing locations, and when configured SecretRefs silently fall back to env credentials.
* `openclaw doctor` now emits structured warnings for SecretRef env fallback cases that previously only appeared in runtime/gateway logs.
* No config schema, runtime enforcement, or secret resolution behavior changes.
* Deep security audit scope is unchanged: archived workspace skills remain included in code-safety scans.

## Evidence

**Focused tests (3 files, 8 tests):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts \
    src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts \
    src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts \
    src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

 ✓ security audit plugin load path findings > returns no findings when plugins.load.paths is unset    71ms
 ✓ security audit plugin load path findings > flags world-writable configured plugin load paths       128ms
 ✓ security audit plugin load path findings > flags missing configured plugin load paths               35ms
 ✓ security audit SecretRef env fallback findings > maps shared diagnostics to a security audit finding  1ms
 ✓ collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics > flags gateway token SecretRef env fallback                 57ms
 ✓ collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics > includes runtime web-tool fallback warnings                 0ms
 ✓ collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics > skips gateway token fallback when auth mode is password     0ms
 ✓ collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics > returns empty diagnostics when SecretRef resolves normally  0ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Duration  2.05s
```

**Real behavior proof (programmatic, redacted config):**

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-audit-load-paths-secretref.mjs

=== openclaw security audit (programmatic, redacted config) ===
[info] plugins.load_paths.trust_boundary: Explicit plugin load paths configured
[warn] plugins.load_paths.missing: Plugin load path is missing or inaccessible
[warn] secrets.ref_env_fallback_used: Configured SecretRef fell back to environment credentials
  ok: audit reports plugins.load_paths.missing for configured missing path
  ok: audit reports secrets.ref_env_fallback_used for unresolved gateway token SecretRef

=== doctor-style SecretRef fallback diagnostic (shared helper) ===
GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK @ gateway.auth.token: gateway.auth.token SecretRef could not be resolved; runtime is using OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN env fallback.
  ok: shared diagnostic includes GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK

=== inactive auth mode: password (no false gateway fallback) ===
  ok: password auth mode skips inactive gateway token SecretRef fallback warning

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

**Environment:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0

**What was not tested:** Live gateway startup with real SecretRef providers; the `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` health check wires the same `collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics` helper (see `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts:284–299`), verified locally via the shared diagnostic proof above.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.ts` | New config-layer load path risk collector |
| `src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.ts` | Maps shared diagnostics to security audit finding |
| `src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` | Shared runtime/doctor/audit diagnostic helper |
| `src/security/audit.ts` | Wires both collectors into runSecurityAudit |
| `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts` | Lazy exports for new async collectors; restores `includeArchived: true` in deep skill code-safety scan |
| `src/security/audit.nondeep.runtime.ts` | Facade exports for loaded audit collectors |
| `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts` | Adds `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` health check |
| `*.test.ts` | Regression tests for both surfaces |

## AI-assisted disclosure

* AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
* Human-run real behavior proof from local setup
